elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1: "This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York." — the Singapore choice-of-law words are replaced with New York law.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Retained 28.2: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction... Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court..." The only carve-out is temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum; the conflicting Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction words in 28.1 are deleted, so no contradictory retained sentence remains.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 selects the laws of the State of New York, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is the preferred (superior) position, so the fallback level is simply unused.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum in retained 28.2 is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Consistent with the preferred level being taken instead.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York law is inserted in 28.1 and the already-favourable exclusive New York County merits forum in 28.2 (with a customary temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out only) is retained unchanged.

Minimal: the edit touches only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 and deletes the Singapore exclusive-forum phrase, which is necessary because retaining it would leave a direct contradiction with 28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or other extras were added, and no Customer-favourable language elsewhere was removed.

Preserves intent: 28.2's personal-jurisdiction submission, venue/forum-non-conveniens waiver, and injunctive-relief carve-out survive intact; 28.3's escalation mechanic is untouched; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created (the injunctive carve-out still references confidential information/intellectual property, and Confidential Information remains defined at 16.1).

Fallback level is not met and does not need to be: the drafter took the higher preferred position, and the comment correctly flags Delaware, California, or England and Wales with corresponding courts as acceptable alternatives without conceding them in operative language.
Deterministic gates (operation applies, accepted governing law, minimality, element coverage) all pass and are confirmed in substance on the rendered text.
